title: Minilaunch checklist + 24h rollout schedule (jun 2026) - wip
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first checklist and hour-by-hour 24h rollout schedule for small feature releases ("minilaunches") that touch API routing, model variant swaps, or client-side flag flips. Goal: predictable, low-friction rollout with clear handoffs and a brutally simple rollback path.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Use for releases that do not require data migrations or infra changes (no DB schema, no stateful migrations).
- Intended for single-team launches or cross-team launches with a single control owner.
- Not for full-product launches or infra-wide capacity changes.

Owner and shift roles (single-point contacts):
- Release Owner: Aisha Kumar (primary contact for go/no-go, communication)
- Ops Lead: Diego Martinez (runs the rollout timeline, triggers traffic shifts)
- QA Smoke: Priya Shah (runs preflight and post-shift smoke tests)
- On-call Eng: Liam O'Neill (pager responder for incidents during +4h window)
- Comms: Product PM (named per launch, usually on rotation)

Pre-flight (T-minus >48h) - checklist items (do before day-of):
- Announce release window in #release-ops two business days prior with scope and rollback plan.
- Create a short Jira release ticket with checklist and link to this doc.
- Verify metric dashboards: latency, error-rate, token-consumption, model-fallback-count. Capture baseline snapshots.
- Confirm canaries exist for this route and are healthy for 24+ hours.
- Run the smoke test harness in staging and record run screenshots/logs.
- Ensure runbook has escalation path and runbook entry exists in PagerDuty.
- Confirm team staffing for day-of windows (+1h ramp, +4h watch, +24h handoff).

Artifact readiness (T-minus 24h):
- Release bundle is built and pinned in the artifact registry (artifact id listed in Jira).
- Model versions pinned in config and validated via dry-run in staging.
- Feature flag toggles created with owner and reverse toggle documented.
- Telemetry probes added to measure quality regressions (top-3 prompt sets).
- Alert thresholds reviewed and agreed (critical: error-rate >1%; warning: latency p50 +50% above baseline).

Day-of: 24h hour-by-hour compact schedule (times are relative to T+0 release moment)
Pre-shift (T-60 to T-15 min):
- T-60: Ops Lead posts "Release starting in 60m" message in #release-ops; callout of watchers and pager.
- T-45: Final artifact check: checksum, config values, environment variables.
- T-30: QA Smoke runs golden-path tests in canary environment; results posted.
- T-15: Go/No-Go sync: Release Owner confirms with Ops Lead, QA, On-call.
- T-5: Ops Lead runs a short traffic snapshot and baseline measurement (p50/p95 latency, error-rate).

T+0: Initial traffic shift (micro-canary)
- Action: Shift 1% of production traffic to new variant/model/route.
- Who: Ops Lead executes routing change and records command/commit id.
- QA: Run smoke test on the 1% cohort (Priya).
- Observability: Watch latency, error-rate, model-fallback, and cost metrics for 10m.
- Comms: Release Owner posts T+0 status (1% shifted) and links to dashboards.

T+10m: Micro-canary review
- If metrics within warning bounds: proceed.
- If metric shows regression but not critical: pause and consult Release Owner & On-call.
- If critical (alerts firing): rollback to 0% immediately (ops command) and open incident.

T+15m: Ramp to 10%
- Action: Ops Lead ramps traffic to 10%.
- QA: Run full smoke suite against 10% path (includes latency-sensitive flows).
- Telemetry: Start rapid-quality checks on top prompt sets; compare to baseline.

T+30m: 10% review and ramp decision
- If healthy, Ramp to 50%. If degraded, hold and investigate.

T+45m: Ramp to 50% (if green)
- Action: Ramp to 50% and run broader synthetic traffic to exercise edge cases.
- On-call standing by for 15m for quick fixes.

T+60m: Full ramp to 100%
- Action: Ops Lead flips final routing to 100%. Document the change and commit id.
- QA: Final regression smoke run across major customer flows.
- Comms: Post release note in #release-ops and update Jira with final status.

Post-ramp watch window (+0 to +4h):
- Who watches: Ops Lead + On-call + QA + Product PM.
- Tasks: Monitor telemetry for increased errors, latency drift, or quality regression.
- If a regression is detected: follow the rollback checklist below.

Post-launch stabilization (+4h to +24h):
- Continue sampling production traffic for quality issues; run scheduled evaluation harness at +6h and +18h.
- Ops Lead to collect first 24h metrics snapshot and annotate anomalies.
- If none critical, sign off to hand off to normal support at +24h.

Rollback checklist (be ruthless, go back to previous known-good state):
- Trigger: any of these triggers rollback immediately: error-rate >1% sustained for 5m; p95 latency >2x baseline for 10m; automated quality-reporter flags severe drop in top prompt set scores.
- Execute rollback command (Ops Lead) and confirm route is back to previous commit/model id.
- Post-rollback: run smoke tests to validate restoration.
- Open postmortem ticket and annotate time-of-failure, root cause hypothesis, and immediate mitigations.
- Notify users and stakeholders per comms template below.

Communication templates (short):
- Pre-start (T-60): "Minilaunch starting in 60m. Owner: Aisha Kumar. Watchers: Diego, Priya, Liam. Link: {jira}."
- T+0 update: "T+0: 1% traffic shifted to new variant. Watching latency & errors: {dashboard_link}."
- Successful completion: "Minilaunch complete: 100% traffic at T+1h. No critical regressions observed in first 4h. See {jira} for notes."
- Rollback notice: "Rollback executed at T+XX due to {reason}. Route restored to {commit/model}. Investigation ticket: {jira} (owner)."

Quick smoke checklist (run at each ramp checkpoint):
- Happy-path text generation end-to-end for three sample prompts.
- Embeddings pipeline quick run and size/latency check.
- Authorization/403 edge-case test.
- Rate limit behavior sanity check.
- Telemetry events produced for each critical code path evaluated.

Known failure modes to watch (and quick mitigation):
- Token-cost spike: revert to previous model variant and throttle batch sizes.
- Incomplete KV cache warmup causing latency: reduce concurrency or roll back.
- Silent quality regression (low-level score drift): pause and re-route small percentage away from new variant.

Post-release notes draft (to be pasted into Jira/Confluence):
- Summary: Small feature rollout (minilaunch) for route /v1/generate: swapped default model to model-x-quantized.
- Scope: client-facing inference routing change. No schema/data migrations.
- Timeline: Initial canary T+0 at 2026-06-07T14:00Z, full ramp at T+60m.
- Outcome: Full rollout completed; no critical incidents; p95 latency +8% (within target); cost per token +1.2%.
- Follow-ups: run thorough eval on additional prompt sets; consider reducing batch sizing to recover p95.

Open questions / items to resolve before finalizing:
- Do we need a staged comms blast to customers for this tiny change? (Product PM input)
- Add a small synthetic test that covers a failing edge-case seen in last regression (see notes in Jira).
- Should we augment alerting to include quality-regression detector for top customers?

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the day-of checklist short and action-oriented. Avoid extra meetings — use Slack and direct pings.
- For minilaunches, favor fast rollback over long debugging during ramp.
- Capture exact routing commands and commit ids in the Jira ticket for auditability.

Document history:
- 2026-06-05: initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2026-06-06: added hour-by-hour schedule and rollback triggers (Diego)
- 2026-06-07: QA smoke checklist additions and final phrasing tweaks (Priya)
